Subject: Redwood co-sell incentive renewal — proposed term sheet

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re doing well — wanted to kick off the renewal conversation for the AWS co-sell incentive structure that’s scheduled to expire at the end of September. I’ve attached an updated term sheet with the program we’re proposing for the 10/1–9/30 period (AWS_CoSell_TermSheet_Aug2026.pdf).

High level:
- Base co-sell credit remains at 10% for Standard listings.
- New tiered uplift for Enterprise SKUs: 15% for net-new deals > $250k ARR.
- 6-month performance review clause to allow minor adjustments based on attachment rate and joint pipeline.

We know Redwood is focused on predictable economics for customers so we included a 12-month minimum eligibility window for co-sell credits on announced deals. We’d like to schedule a 30-min alignment call next week to walk through the term sheet and any commercial asks you have.

Can you confirm the right folks on your side to loop in (commercial, legal, finance)? If anything on the sheet is a non-starter please mark it and we’ll come back with a revised version.

Thanks — looking forward to working this through.

Best,
Emily Park
Partner Programs, AWS Marketplace

Thanks Vanessa — quick analysis attached (redwood_co_sell_model.xlsx). Main takeaways:

- If we accept AWS's proposed base (10%) + enterprise uplift (15%): estimated incremental rev credit to partners ~ +4.2% of gross ARR for FY27 vs current program. Upside concentrated in three accounts where we have active pipeline.
- Concern: the 12-month eligibility floor materially delays the time when customers can take advantage of marketplace consolidation & transfer credits; that increases our gross-to-net timing risk and could push recognized revenue later by ~90–120 days for co-sell-sourced deals.
- Counter suggestions:
  * Keep Enterprise uplift but apply to "closed-won after listing" rather than "announced deal" to reduce ambiguity.
  * Propose a 6-month eligibility floor instead of 12-months with a performance review clause at 6 months.
  * Add carve-outs for partner-originated renewals (we should not lose credit on renewals we brought to market).

I highlighted cells in the model showing the sensitivity to deal size thresholds. I also flagged language we should ask AWS to clarify in the term sheet (definitions and the recapture clause).

Adding legal perspective and next steps. Quick notes on language risk:

- "Net-new" must be defined precisely. We should insist on "customer with no prior commercial contract for the same product family in the past 24 months" or similar.
- Recapture: the proposed recapture language is broad; request a cap (e.g., limited to amounts erroneously paid due to fraud or clear data errors) and a 6-month lookback window for adjustments.
- Minimum eligibility: 6 months is reasonable from a controls perspective; 12 months is excessive operationally.

Recommended next steps:
1) Vanessa to propose our counter in writing: accept base 10% for Standard, accept Enterprise uplift 15% but only for closed-won deals (not announced), change eligibility floor to 6 months, add carve-out for partner-originated renewals, and cap recapture to clear errors.
2) Schedule a 30-min alignment call with Emily and their legal lead — suggested times: Tue 08/24 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 08/25 11:00–11:30 PT. I can join both.
3) Marissa/Marcus to confirm modeled impact and bring one-page summary for the call.

I’ve cc’ed Emily to keep AWS in the loop; Vanessa, if you want me to draft the counters, I can take a first pass and share the text for review.

Thanks,
